name: Local complementation simplification
summary: An internal spider with phase ±π/2 can be removed by complementing the connectivity of its neighbours.
description:
In a graph-like diagram, an internal spider with phase π/2 (or −π/2) can be removed. Every pair of its neighbours that was connected becomes disconnected and vice versa, and π/2 is subtracted from (or added to) the phase of every neighbour. This is the graph-theoretic operation of *local complementation*.

The rule is derived from the local complementation rule for graph states of Duncan & Perdrix, followed by spider fusion. It is one of the two main simplification rules of PyZX, together with [pivoting](../pivot/).
parameter_notes: n is the number of neighbours (shown for n = 3). The neighbours may have any number of further legs and edges.
